thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime p99 latency jumped 4x after release v2026.03.17. Autoscale healthy but tail latency rising. Auto-pages sent to #incidents and oncall.

mira: i'm on it, looking at tracing now. paging dan for kernel selector logs.

dan: joining, saw similar in canary graphs, kernels falling back to generic path.

kevin: customer telemetry shows increased 503s for heavy-chat routes, starting ~14:02 UTC.

mira: quick ask — is rollback allowed or try feature-flag kill first? we want minimal customer impact.

sam: product — we have 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated affected, high priority. prefer kill-switch if it stabilizes.

lia: digging into batcher metrics. Batch window shrank, microbatches spiking -> more kernel thrash. looks like new scheduling change from rollout.

dan: confirmed kernel selector fell back due to `seq_len_est` variance. fallback to slow kernels increases token latency.

mira: ops-bot run preflight checks and surface node-level evictions pls.

ops-bot: preflight checks: 12/120 nodes showing high kernel_fallback_rate, 29% increase in microbatch_count, no memory OOMs.

kevin: logs: `kernel_selector.cpp: line 482: fallback_reason=seq_len_mismatch, selected_kernel=generic_attention` repeated per-request.

mira: attempt soft mitigation — disable new scheduling flag on canary first. `/flag set scheduling_v2=false --env=canary`

ops-bot: flag set scheduling_v2=false on canary successfully. metrics in 2m.

lia: after flag flip canary latency p95 improved ~15%, but production still bad.

mira: escalate to kill-switch for rollout: `/feature_flag kill rollout_scheduling_v2` — this will stop the rollout and route traffic to previous release.

sam: authorized — do it. communicate to customers.

mira: executing kill-switch now.

ops-bot: feature_flag `rollout_scheduling_v2` killed. routing reverted to stable scheduler. starting traffic rebalancing.

dan: seeing immediate drop in kernel_fallback_rate on prod nodes. p95 down ~30% within 90s.

kevin: customer 1's telemetry back to normal, still watching.

lia: batching stabilized — microbatch_count back to expected distribution.

mira: good. i'm going to initiate controlled rollback of the release agent to v2026.03.16 to be safe: `deploy rollback --release v2026.03.16 --scope=cluster-wide`

ops-bot: rollback started (job id 98765). ETA ~6m for full cutover, will preserve active sessions.

dan: prepare postmortem notes: likely root cause is scheduler change + seq_len distribution shift causing kernel selector heuristics to choose fallback paths. we'll capture evictions, batch histograms, and canary sample traces.

sam: product — i'll draft customer comms: "We experienced elevated latency impacting some routes after a rollout. We killed the rollout and rolled back; service is recovering. Investigating root cause and will follow up."

mira: handoff to dan for overnight mitigation and RCA. dan you're oncall now.

dan: taking the on-call. will run deeper heap of traces and collect kernel selector metrics. leaving a note in #eng-runtime runbook.

kevin: thumbs up, i'll help with perf tests to reproduce locally.

lia: saving batch histograms and KV cache stats to S3: `s3://redwood-incident/3141592653/`

ops-bot: rollback complete. p95 and error rates stable.

mira: incident closed for active mitigation, keeping thread open for RCA/pm follow-ups. :thumbsup:
